text:
ella: Running the onboarding sampleapp today and hit a weird quota/backpressure interaction during pagination. Not the usual 429 flood — we see inflight counters jump and duplicate page fetches when the auth token rotates mid-batch. Repro locally.

omar: Can you paste a tiny log extract?

ella: sure:
```
INFO page=3 inflight=5 state=pending-auth status=401
INFO auth refresh start id=auth-11
INFO auth refresh done id=auth-12
INFO replay page=3 inflight=6 duplicate-fetch
WARN upstream soft-429 backlog=30
```
You can see inflight climbs when the SDK replays the request. Looks like the original waiting attempt wasn't reconciled with the replay.

lucy: Is the client using a simple inflight counter or a logical slot model? If it's the straight counter then an internal retry path can accidentally acquire again.

ella: It's simple windowing in the sampleapp client lib. The auth middleware intercepts 401 and replays the original promise; the windowing code treats waiting promises as holding a slot, and the replay path acquires a fresh slot.

omar: Two mitigation ideas: (1) auth wrapper releases the slot before refreshing and re-acquires afterward (fast hack, but risks other callers stealing the slot), (2) implement logical leases/id per logical request so retries reuse the same logical slot, or (3) change windowing to have reserved vs active counts so a request blocked on auth doesn't count against active throughput.

lucy: My vote is for logical-id leases. It keeps a 1:1 mapping of logical requests to slots and plays nice with background prefetch and long polling. Also add an X-Logical-Id header to aid server-side dedupe.

ella: agree. Proposed pattern:
```js
const logicalId = uuid();
await window.reserve(logicalId); // reserves a slot but not counted as active
try {
  await sendWithAuth(req, {logicalId}); // retries reuse logicalId
} finally {
  await window.release(logicalId);
}
```
Where window.promote(logicalId) increments active_count only when the request actually starts sending.

omar: If we take this path we should add a tiny integration test in sampleapp that toggles auth to 401 mid-run and asserts active_count <= windowSize and that server sees consistent logical ids. I can own the SDK change once test is in.

lucy: I'll add the failing harness and a trace. Also draft a quick blurb for the onboarding guide explaining reserved slots vs naive counters so new users don't hit this trap.

devex-bot: Created ticket RDW-5204: "onboard-sampleapp: inflight overshoot during token-rotation; implement logical leases and X-Logical-Id" and linked branch r/patch/logical-leases. Assigned: omar (sdk impl), lucy (test + docs).

ella: Thanks — pushing the harness now. If we standardize logical-leases across SDKs it should reduce a chunk of noisy support cases about mysterious soft 429s during onboarding. :thumbsup:
